segments.source: Big Trouble is a sensible first trial when you want a familiar flavor direction for several brewing methods and do not specifically want the roaster's darkest option. The purchase works best as a small-bag comparison against your current coffee. Its changing recipe and your brewing routine matter more than its reassuring name.

segments.context: Image: Counter Culture Coffee. Official Counter Culture product photograph, used to identify the coffee; not a Coffeedant tasting photograph.

segments.source: Choose Forty-Six when the job is a familiar dark-roast coffee for milk drinks and you are willing to follow a blend that changes its components. Start with a small bag and judge it in your normal drink. A dark label alone does not guarantee low bitterness, low caffeine or compatibility with an automatic machine.
